# core/lines.bastio

<!-- Generated by tests/libref.py from core/lines.bastio: edit the source, then run tests/libref.py --write. -->

Splitting text into lines.

A line ends at `\n`, and a `\r` just before it belongs to the terminator.
The last line needs no terminator, but a terminator at the very end of the
text does not start another, empty line, so `a\nb\n` and `a\nb` are both
two lines and an empty text has none. A blank line in the middle is an
empty span. Lines are spans of the text, so nothing is copied.

What is proved: every span lies inside the text, and none holds a `\n`.

`import "core/lines.bastio";` also loads [core/option.bastio](core-option.md), [core/bytes.bastio](core-bytes.md).

| Function | |
| --- | --- |
| [`lines_split`](#lines_split) | The lines of `b`, in order. |

Every example below is built, verified and run by `tests/run.sh`. An `assert` in one is proved at compile time from the contracts above it.

## Functions

### `lines_split`

```bastio
fn lines_split(b: &Bytes) -> Vec[Span]
  ensures lines_ok(result, b)
```

The lines of `b`, in order.

Example:

```bastio
let b = bfrom("one\r\ntwo\n\nfour");
let ls = lines_split(b);
let mut ok = vec_len(ls) == 4;
if ok {
  let l0 = vec_get(ls, 0);
  let l1 = vec_get(ls, 1);
  let l2 = vec_get(ls, 2);
  let l3 = vec_get(ls, 3);
  ok = bytes_span_eq_str(b, l0.start, l0.end, "one")
    && bytes_span_eq_str(b, l1.start, l1.end, "two")
    && l2.start == l2.end
    && bytes_span_eq_str(b, l3.start, l3.end, "four");
}
vec_free(ls);
let e = balloc(0);
let none = lines_split(e);
let zero = vec_len(none) == 0;
vec_free(none);
bfree(e);
bfree(b);
if !ok || !zero { return 1; }
```

## Specification functions

### `lines_ok`

```bastio
spec fn lines_ok(v: &Vec[Span], b: &Bytes) -> bool {
  forall i: u64 :: i < vlen(v) ==> span_in(vget(v, i), b)
    && (forall k: u64 :: vget(v, i).start <= k && k < vget(v, i).end ==> bget(b, k) != 10)
}
```

Every span in `v` lies inside `b` and holds no newline.
